answer.location_description: Top-right corner of the image, the first few rows at the far right columns (roughly rows 0-4, columns 19-23), strongest along column 23 and row 0.
answer.mechanism: About 12 layer-1 units carry learned spatial structure; the other 20 look like untrained noise. Eight of them (1, 2, 8, 10, 18, 20, 24, 28; all negative bias) have large positive weights in the top-right corner. They feed layer-2 units 3, 10 and 12 strongly and positively (e.g. u10: unit18 +81, unit1 +73, unit24 +66; u12: unit10 +89; u3: unit10 +86, unit2 +81), and those layer-2 units carry positive output weights (+65, +73, +75). The four benign-detecting units (23, 27, 29, 31; large positive bias) have negative weights in the same corner. They feed layer-2 units 1 and 13, which have negative output weights (-99, -80). Brightness in the top-right corner therefore both excites the malignant pathway and suppresses the benign pathway, pushing the logit positive.
answer.evidence: Malignant-side units peak in the top-right corner, among the largest positive weights they have. Unit 1: r0c23 = 61, r2c23 = 45. Unit 10: r0c22-23 = 42, 52; r3c23 = 43; r4c23 = 56. Unit 20: r0c20-23 = 32, 42, 38, 43; r3c23 = 45. Unit 24: r1-r3 c23 = 30, 35, 48. Unit 28: r0c20-21 = 52, 47; r2c22-23 = 37, 45. Unit 2: column 23 rows 0-5 = 24, 28, 33, 42, 32, 42. Unit 8: r0c23 = 45, r5c23 = 44. Benign-side units are negative at the same pixels while positive at the top-left of row 0. Unit 27: r0c18-23 = -20, -39, -36, -35, -48, -38 and r4c23 = -49, versus r0c0-3 = 19, -9, 26, 28. Unit 23: r0c19-23 = -29, -6, -29, -30, -43 and r1c23 = -33, versus left side +20, +9, +17. Units 29 and 31 likewise have r0 right side negative (e.g. -32, -26) and left side positive. This left/right asymmetry in a corner far from the centered nodule is not explained by nodule anatomy, which should be roughly rotation-symmetric.
answer.main_feature: The genuine signal is a center-surround nodule-morphology pattern: malignant units have negative weights on a ring around the nodule (about rows 5-17) with positive lobes extending outward, responding to irregular or spiculated margins and tissue reaching beyond the nodule. Benign units respond to the opposite pattern, a compact nodule surrounded by clean dark lung.
